summary: Fumihiko Sueki works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura, Yoshiro Tamura, and Kyosho Hayashima, later serving as professor there (1995–2009) and at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (~2009–2015).
Fumihiro Okada specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (attested 2015) and held a post at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

Fumimaro Watanabe specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University and the University of Toronto under Anthony Kennedy Warder and Hammalawa Saddhatissa. He later served as professor at Kindai University (1981) and Aichi Gakuin University (1987).
Fumio Enomoto is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a research assistant at Kyoto University (~1981–1985) and as a professor at Osaka University (~1999–2020).

Fumio Masutani was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who earned degrees from the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1952–1966) and Taisho University (~1966–1973), and served as president of Tsuru University (1969–1971).
Fumio Matsuda works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He has held posts at Komazawa University and the Association for the Study of Indian Religions (attested 1997).

Fumio Ouchi specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. He completed a doctorate at Otani University, where he served as associate professor (~1988–1999) and professor (~1999–2013).

Fumio Shoji specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Rissho University from ~1998 to 2008 and later held posts there as an assistant professor (~2012–2017) and associate professor (~2017).
Fumio Tamamuro is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Meiji University (~1953–1957) and later held a post there from ~1968 to 2006.

Futoshi Omae works in Indology and philosophy. He held posts as a lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 1990–1991) and taught at Shimane Prefectural Junior College of Nursing (attested 1997) and Shimane International Junior College (attested 1998).

Futoshi Takehashi specializes in Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies at Otani University (attested 1992) and served as a research assistant at the Shinshu Otani-ha Research Institute from 1995 to 1997.
Fuyuan Luo is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar. As of 2026, he is a PhD student at the University of Cambridge studying under Adam Yuet Chau.

Fyodor Buslaev worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at the Faculty of History and Philology of Moscow University (~1834–1838) and took up a post at Moscow State University in 1846.

Fyodor Shcherbatskoy worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Ivan Minayev and Sergey Oldenburg, and later under Georg Bühler and Hermann Jacobi, serving as a professor at Saint Petersburg State University (~1900–1941).

Félix Nève was an Indologist and linguist. He earned a doctorate from KU Leuven (~1834–1838) and studied under Christian Lassen, Friedrich Wilhelm Thiersch, and Eugène Burnouf, later serving as professor at KU Leuven from 1841.
G. B. Palsule was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He held posts at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1957) and Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1987).
G. K. Jenkins was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at Bloxham School (~1932–1937), he held a post at the British Museum from 1947 to 1978.

G. P. Malalasekera specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of London and SOAS under Caroline Rhys Davids and William Stede, later serving as lecturer and Dean of Oriental Studies at the University of Ceylon.
G. Srinivasa Murti worked in Indology and served as director of the Adyar Library and Research Centre (attested 1938–1949 and 1971).

G. Thomas Tanselle studied at Yale University (~1951–1955). He taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1960–1978), served as vice president of the John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation (1978–2006), and was adjunct professor of English at Columbia University (~1978–2007).
